bakeoff: ETA 3-arm transcription/diarization bake-off (Mac Mini vs hosted pyannote.ai + WhisperAI)

arms.B_current_mini: Production Mac Mini transcripts + local diarization (read-only, not re-run)
arms.C_hybrid: pyannote.ai (precision-3) diarization + Arm B's existing transcripts

preconditions.whisperai_direct_api_question: Does WhisperAI offer a programmatic API/SDK ETA's Vercel code could call directly (not via this MCP)?
preconditions.evidence: No REST endpoint, API key, or SDK surfaced anywhere in the WhisperAI MCP tool set or get_account metadata; only usable via this MCP integration (transcribe_url/start_upload + get_transcript polling). Any hosted-WhisperAI path requires keeping this MCP/agent layer, not a direct backend call.

models_used.diarization_local: existing Mini local diarization engine (unchanged, read-only)

methodology_limitations: WhisperAI was tested on a ~300s audio sample per window vs the full ~900s canonical window (partial-audio-sample limitation) -- CER/WER via jiwer was judged not meaningful under this mismatch and was replaced with qualitative hallucination/quality flags per-window, per the task's own allowance to report a blocked stage and continue.

pyannote diarization was run on a 30-minute over-fetch per window in this bake-off (not the canonical 15-minute span); frame-agreement scoring against local spans is unaffected because local spans only populate frames within their true ~900s coverage, but the pyannote cost figures below distinguish 'actual bake-off cost' from 'projected canonical-window cost'.

doc-ID (local_id_doc_ppmku68m) check is unsatisfiable with available data for all 20 windows -- no retrievable enrolled voiceprint clip existed to test hosted speaker-ID against; reported as a blocked stage, not a failure of pyannote identify itself.
WhisperAI ingestion is rate-limited to 5 calls/min; 3/20 windows hard-failed at the transcription stage.

arm_A_whisperai_quality_tally.pattern: Failures/hallucinations cluster on Kannada/Tamil/Telugu-majority or 'thin' (near-silent) windows; clean output clusters on English/Hindi-majority windows.

language_mix_local_pipeline.note: span-count weighted across 20 windows, local (Arm B/C) ASR engine routing only

latency.whisperai_note: not individually logged per-window by the MCP; ingest bounded by 5 calls/min rate limit

cost.pyannote_identify_cost: not incurred -- no enrolled voiceprint available to test against (see doc-ID limitation)
cost.whisperai_cost: not exposed via MCP -- flat 'pro' plan, unlimited minutes per get_account, no per-minute/hour price surfaced
cost.arm_C_hybrid_marginal_cost_note: pyannote diarization only (Arm B transcripts are already-produced/sunk cost); ~=EUR0.028/canonical window

doctor_id.note: local_id_doc_ppmku68m is False for all 20 windows; blocked/not-testable given available data, not a pyannote failure

listen_windows_largest_disagreement.reason: lowest local-vs-pyannote frame agreement (0.3607); also among worst WhisperAI hallucination/garble outputs
2nd-lowest frame agreement (0.4786); heavy Kannada/mixed-language content, largest local/pyannote speaker-count spread
extreme speaker-count mismatch (local=1 vs pyannote=9) despite moderate frame agreement; 'thin' near-silent activity; WhisperAI hallucination flagged
severe WhisperAI hallucination on Kannada-majority content (kn:17 spans) despite acceptable diarization agreement -- ASR-arm divergence, not diarization
WhisperAI hallucination flagged; frame agreement not computable (insufficient overlapping speech) -- a genuine coverage gap, not just disagreement

recommendation.verdict: HYBRID (Arm C) for diarization now; keep local ASR; do not switch transcription to WhisperAI
reasoning: pyannote diarization is cheap (EUR0.028/canonical window), fast (p50 20.2s vs local ASR's own 161.4s), and improves speaker-count resolution in cases where local under-counts speakers, but only ~62% median frame agreement with local -- treat as a diarization upgrade, not a doc-ID solution (doc-ID remains blocked pending voiceprint enrollment).

WhisperAI transcription has a 45% problem rate (30% hallucination/garble + 15% hard failure) concentrated exactly on the Kannada/Tamil/Telugu content that makes up ~40% of ETA's real clinic-room language mix -- switching primary transcription to WhisperAI would regress quality on close to half the caseload.

WhisperAI has no direct/programmatic API -- adopting it keeps ETA dependent on this MCP integration layer rather than a first-party backend call, adding operational risk for a component that already underperforms on Indic content.

Net: move diarization to pyannote.ai (Arm C) for cost/speed/speaker-count benefit; keep the Mini's local multi-engine ASR (whisper/sravaani/indicconformer) as the transcription arm; revisit WhisperAI only if/when its Indic-language accuracy improves and a real programmatic API exists.
